Assumptions: output ceramics 2 x 25 uF (47 uF derated at 5 V), 3 mOhm ESR; input 2 x 2.2 uF; L1 8.2 uH, 17 mOhm; D13 a generic 5 A / 60 V Schottky; supply 20 mOhm. See the docstring of `buck.py`.

What this does and does not show: it checks the converter's DESIGN (the values: output voltage, switching frequency, compensation, start-up) with TI's model. It does not include the board's layout (track inductance, switch-node ringing, noise), the real diode's forward voltage (the efficiency is somewhat optimistic for that reason), or temperature. The load-step and steady cases start from a preset state and settle for their first 0.3 ms; the measurements skip it.
